feed.title: G.M.’s and Toyota’s U.S. first-quarter sales fell sharply as a chip shortage persisted.
feed.summary: General Motors and Toyota Motor experienced significant declines in their U.S. first-quarter sales due to the ongoing global semiconductor chip shortage. GM's sales dropped 20%, while Toyota's fell 15%, indicating that production disruptions continue to impact the automotive industry. Experts predict that inventory shortages will persist throughout the year, further exacerbated by factors like rising gas prices and the conflict in Ukraine.

feed.title: California approves $11.7M vehicle-to-grid pilots in PG&E footprint
feed.summary: The California Public Utilities Commission has approved $11.7 million in vehicle-to-grid (VGI) pilot programs for Pacific Gas & Electric Co. These pilots aim to integrate electric vehicles into the grid, provide backup power, and reduce EV ownership costs through bidirectional charging technology. The initiatives include residential, commercial, and microgrid programs to test incentives and rate designs for scaling VGI technologies.

feed.title: Tech firm Applied Materials considers Hutto for $2.4 billion facility, hundreds of jobs
feed.summary: Applied Materials, a tech firm, is evaluating Hutto, Texas, as a potential site for a new $2.4 billion research and development facility, which could create hundreds of jobs. The Hutto Independent School District is considering tax breaks for the project, known as "Project Acropolis." This potential expansion highlights Central Texas's growing high-tech sector, following other major investments by companies like Samsung and Tesla.

feed.title: Samsung Asset Management gets 20% equity stake in Amplify
feed.summary: Samsung Asset Management has acquired a 20% equity stake in Amplify. The deal was reported on April 1, 2022, and was featured in Pensions & Investments.

feed.title: Tesla delivers record 310,048 vehicles globally in 'exceptionally difficult' Q1, Elon Musk says
feed.summary: Tesla announced record vehicle deliveries of 310,048 globally in the first quarter, despite what Elon Musk described as an "exceptionally difficult" period. The company achieved this milestone, continuing its growth trajectory even in challenging market conditions.

feed.title: Why Big Companies Like Tesla and Amazon Are Splitting Stocks
feed.summary: This article explains what a stock split is and why major companies like Tesla, Amazon, and Alphabet execute them. It delves into the financial and psychological reasons behind stock splits, such as making shares more accessible to a wider range of investors and signaling positive future performance, despite the total market capitalization remaining unchanged. The piece also discusses the impact of stock splits on retail investors and highlights the strong post-split performance of such stocks.

feed.title: Hertz plans to buy 65,000 EVs from Polestar over five years
feed.summary: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. announced plans to purchase 65,000 electric vehicles from Polestar over the next five years, indicating a bet on increasing EV curiosity among renters and a desire to diversify beyond Tesla. This deal follows Hertz's previous announcement to buy 100,000 Teslas, significantly expanding its electric fleet to appeal to corporate clients and ride-share drivers while potentially reducing maintenance costs. The purchase provides a stable revenue stream for Polestar as it expands its market presence and prepares for a public debut.

feed.title: Tesla's factory opening is expected to draw thousands, so Del Valle is closing schools early
feed.summary: The Del Valle Independent School District is closing schools early due to an anticipated 15,000 attendees at the grand opening of Tesla's Gigafactory in eastern Travis County. The event, dubbed a "Cyber Rodeo," is expected to cause significant traffic congestion, prompting the district to adjust dismissal times for elementary, middle, and high schools. This move aims to mitigate traffic issues as students head home while the event starts.

feed.title: 3 Reasons Why People Are Adding Digital Assets Exposure
feed.summary: The article discusses three key reasons investors are adding digital asset ETFs like SATO and BLKC to their portfolios. These reasons include digital assets being a transformative and growing economic force, their potential to hedge against inflation due to finite supply (like Bitcoin), and their ability to further diversify a portfolio, reducing concentration risk.

feed.title: Not just Tesla: Hertz expands EV plan
feed.summary: Hertz announced its plan to buy up to 65,000 electric vehicles from Polestar by 2027, marking its second major EV purchase after its deal with Tesla. This move is praised by EV advocates as it provides more opportunities for the public to experience driving electric cars through rentals. The new purchase also helps boost the Polestar brand, which plans to start producing its Polestar 3 model in South Carolina later this year.

feed.title: Stellantis says direct sales model could be 'win-win-win,' but dealers aren't sure
feed.summary: Stellantis is exploring a direct sales model, similar to Tesla, to simplify the car-buying process and reduce delivery costs. While the company believes this could be a "win-win-win," its dealers are hesitant about the potential shift. Other traditional automakers like Volvo and Ford are also moving towards more online-focused models while still utilizing their dealer networks for sales and repairs.

feed.title: Cambria Hotel Austin Airport opens in Texas, US
feed.summary: The Cambria Hotel Austin Airport has opened in Austin, Texas, marking the brand's sixth property in the state. Developed by W2 SF Airport Hospitality Business LP, the hotel features 127 rooms, multi-purpose indoor/outdoor spaces, including an outdoor pool, spa-style bathrooms, and an onsite restaurant and bar. A second Cambria hotel is planned for downtown Austin next summer.

feed.title: GM, Honda unveil plan to jointly develop ‘affordable’ EVs
feed.summary: General Motors and Honda Motor Co. announced a partnership to jointly develop affordable electric vehicles for major global markets, starting with North America in 2027. This collaboration, which will utilize GM's Ultium EV battery architecture, aims to produce millions of vehicles, primarily small crossover SUVs, and accelerate the transition to EVs for both companies by sharing development costs and technology. The initiative expands on existing collaborations between the two automakers in areas like hydrogen fuel cells and battery technology.

feed.title: REE Automotive Appoints Josh Tech as Chief Operations Officer
feed.summary: REE Automotive (Nasdaq: REE) has appointed Josh Tech, a former Tesla operations leader, as its new Chief Operations Officer. Tech brings over 23 years of experience in product development, manufacturing, and supply chain management, and will oversee REE's global operations, including the launch of integration centers in Austin, Texas, and Coventry, UK, as the company prepares for commercial production of its EV platforms in 2023. Josh replaces Michael Charlton, who will now serve as a strategic advisor.

feed.title: Opinion: Twitter put Elon Musk on the board so he wouldn’t pull another Tesla
feed.summary: Twitter appointed Elon Musk to its board, preventing a potential hostile takeover. This move avoids a repeat of what happened at Tesla, where Musk became the largest shareholder and eventually took control, despite not being a founder. The board seat agreement also restricts Musk from acquiring more than 15% of Twitter's stock.

feed.title: 2 Years Later, FDG and FLV are Soaring
feed.summary: The American Century Focused Dynamic Growth ETF (FDG) and the American Century Focused Large Cap Value ETF (FLV), two active, semi-transparent ETFs, have seen significant growth two years after their launch. Since their inception on March 31, 2020, FDG and FLV have risen by 88.65% and 56.7% respectively, attracting a combined $296.4 million in net investor capital. FDG focuses on rapid-growth companies, while FLV targets value stocks to achieve long-term returns with minimized volatility.

feed.title: 3 Reasons Why Investors Are Adding Digital Assets Exposure
feed.summary: Investors are increasingly adding digital assets to their portfolios for three main reasons: their transformative impact on economic activity, their potential to hedge against inflation (especially assets with finite supplies like Bitcoin), and their ability to further diversify a portfolio. The article highlights ETFs such as SATO and BLKC as ways for investors to gain exposure to this growing asset class.

feed.title: Koch Industries’ Bet on Batteries (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Koch Industries, known for funding groups that question climate change, is investing heavily in battery technology. Its arm, Koch Strategic Platforms, is injecting $30 million into Blue Current, a start-up co-founded by scientist Joseph DeSimone, to develop solid-state silicon batteries. This investment highlights Koch's bet on the growing electric vehicle industry's demand for advanced and safer battery solutions.

feed.title: Is EVgo Stock a Buy?
feed.summary: EVgo (NASDAQ: EVGO) is experiencing impressive growth, with a 52% revenue increase in 2021 and a projected 132% hike for the current year, alongside significant network expansion. The company's stock has outperformed peers, partly due to new partnerships with Subaru and Toyota, and its customer base is growing consistently. While EVgo shows immense growth potential in the EV charging infrastructure market, it is still years away from profitability, making it suitable only for investors with a high risk tolerance.

feed.title: Global Demand Opens Big Opportunity for Mexico Silver Producers
feed.summary: Global demand for strategic metals like silver, copper, and nickel is rapidly increasing due to the production of electric vehicles and solar panels, with some experts predicting up to 14 times higher demand by 2030. This creates a significant opportunity for Mexico, the world's leading silver producer, to leverage its mining assets and meet the growing industrial demand. Companies like Tesla are even investing directly in securing their supply chains for these crucial battery and electronic components.

feed.title: 5 Mind-Blowing Features of Lotus’s First Electric SUV
feed.summary: Lotus has unveiled its first all-electric hyper-SUV, the Eletre, showcasing advanced technology and high performance. Key features include an active front grill for efficient cooling, over 600 horsepower, a 100+ kWh battery with 373 miles of range, and advanced self-driving capabilities using LiDAR sensors. The Eletre also boasts a futuristic interior with multiple screens and sophisticated aerodynamics, signaling Lotus's entry into the electric vehicle market.

feed.title: Flying electric cars are coming — and Oshkosh's airport might be one of the few places to charge them
feed.summary: Volatus Infrastructure has announced plans to build the first permanent electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) vertiport in the Americas at Wittman Regional Airport in Oshkosh. This facility will include a terminal, landing pad, and charging station for electric aircraft, aiming to address the lack of charging infrastructure for emerging eVTOL technology. The project emphasizes Oshkosh's role in aviation innovation and seeks to make electric flying accessible, with an estimated operational date by early fall.

feed.title: China EV maker Nio suspends production due to supply chain disruptions
feed.summary: Chinese electric vehicle (EV) maker Nio has suspended production due to supply chain disruptions caused by China's strict COVID-19 containment measures. The company stated that supplier partners in multiple locations, including Jilin, Shanghai, and Jiangsu, have ceased operations, leading to a halt in car production and delayed deliveries. This situation mirrors similar production suspensions by other major automakers like Tesla and Volkswagen joint ventures in China.

feed.title: The Biggest Reveals from Bitcoin 2022
feed.summary: The Bitcoin 2022 conference in Miami highlighted the early stage of Bitcoin adoption, with comparisons drawn to the internet in 1995. Key announcements included Robinhood rolling out crypto wallets and Lightning Network integration, new jurisdictions like Prospera (Honduras) and Madeira adopting Bitcoin as legal tender, and Strike partnering with major point-of-sale systems like Shopify and McDonald's to facilitate Bitcoin payments. The article emphasizes Bitcoin's potential for mass adoption and its disruptive impact on payment processing.

feed.title: Tesla’s world’s largest battery is moving ahead with expansion
feed.summary: The Tesla Megapack system at Moss Landing, intended to be the world's largest battery, was shut down for months due to a fire investigation. Despite the shutdown, which PG&E and Vistra attribute to incidents unrelated to Tesla's batteries, the companies are moving forward with plans to expand the energy storage system this summer. All parties expect the CPUC to approve the expansion.

feed.title: Honda to spend $64 billion on R&D as it revs up electric ambitions
feed.summary: Honda Motor Co Ltd announced a $64 billion investment in research and development over the next decade, with plans to launch 30 electric vehicle models globally by 2030 and produce 2 million EVs annually. The Japanese automaker aims to gain market share in the growing electric vehicle sector, collaborating with General Motors on production and battery technology, while also emphasizing its continued development of hybrid vehicles.

feed.title: Summary of Honda Briefing on Automobile Electrification Business
feed.summary: Honda announced its strategy for automobile electrification, committing approximately 5 trillion yen over the next decade to electrification and software technologies. The company plans to launch 30 EV models globally by 2030, aiming for over 2 million units in annual production volume. Honda will also invest in solid-state battery production and introduce affordable EVs with GM from 2027.

feed.title: 2022 Hyundai Ioniq 5 Wins Big at World Car Awards
feed.summary: The 2022 Hyundai Ioniq 5 dominated the 2022 World Car Awards, securing three major accolades including the prestigious World Car of the Year, World Electric Vehicle of the Year, and World Car Design of the Year. Hyundai's Luc Donckerwolke was also honored as the 2022 World Car Person of the Year. The awards highlighted significant recognition for electric vehicles, with the Ioniq 5 outperforming competitors like the Kia EV6 and Ford Mustang Mach-E.

feed.title: Futu SG (moomoo), the 1st global digital brokerage, offers $0 platform fee*, $0 market data fee, lifetime $0 commission** on US stocks as markets rally despite conflicts and rising inflation - PR Newswire APAC
feed.summary: Futu Singapore (moomoo) is offering a lifetime $0 commission on US stock trading, along with $0 platform and market data fees, to attract investors amidst market volatility. Data from their platform shows an increasing interest in US stocks among Singaporean investors, particularly those aged 40 and above, with technology and growth stocks being popular choices. The initiative aims to provide enhanced access to US markets and support investors with educational resources and community features.

feed.title: This Chip Maker Supplies Tesla and Apple. Its Stock Could Get a Boost as Shortages Continue.
feed.summary: Dutch-Swiss chip maker STMicroelectronics has experienced a boom in business due to increasing global demand and persistent supply constraints. The company supplies chips to major tech firms like Tesla and Apple. Its stock is projected to benefit from the ongoing semiconductor shortages in the market.

feed.title: Judge finds Tesla liable to Black former worker who alleged bias, but slashes payout
feed.summary: A federal judge has ruled that Tesla is liable to a Black former elevator operator, Owen Diaz, who alleged the company ignored racial abuse at its Fremont factory. While upholding Tesla's liability, the judge significantly reduced a jury's nearly $137 million award to $15 million. Diaz's lawyer plans to appeal the lowered damages, stating the reduced amount does not fully reflect the harm or the reprehensibility of Tesla's conduct.

feed.title: Ford Motor Company Announces F-150 Lightning Arrival Date
feed.summary: Ford Motor Company has announced that the F-150 Lightning electric pickup trucks are scheduled to arrive at dealerships for pre-sold customers around April 26, 2022. The F-150 Lightning has seen tremendous pre-sale success, leading Ford to increase production significantly. Ford will also host a "Job 1" event to celebrate the start of production at the Rouge Electric Vehicle Center.

feed.title: GM CEO Mary Barra talks newest electric vehicle, inflation and competition with Tesla
feed.summary: GM CEO Mary Barra discussed the company's newest EV, the Cadillac LYRIQ, and their commitment to an all-electric future by 2035. She addressed current inflation and high gas prices, noting increased consumer interest in EVs, and outlined GM's plans to expand charging infrastructure. Barra also expressed confidence in GM's ability to compete with Tesla and capture a significant share of the growing EV market.

feed.title: 2022 New York Auto Show: Winners and Losers
feed.summary: The 2022 New York International Auto Show featured many new vehicles, with Cars.com editors identifying both "winners" and "losers" among them. Evaluations covered various models like the Alfa Romeo Tonale, Hyundai Palisade, Kia Niro, Kia Telluride, Jeep Wagoneer L, Nissan Leaf, Nissan Pathfinder Rock Creek, Subaru Outback, VinFast VF 8, and Volkswagen ID. Buzz, focusing on design, practicality, technology, and market relevance. Despite some concerns about specific features or market strategies, several vehicles were praised for their improvements and potential impact.

feed.title: Elon Musk's tweet about taking Tesla private was false, U.S. judge rules
feed.summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that Elon Musk's 2018 tweet about taking Tesla private was false, impacting a shareholder lawsuit. The ruling simplifies the case for investors who claim they lost money due to the tweet, as they will no longer need to prove the falsity of Musk's statements to a jury.

feed.title: NHTSA Opens Two Defect Investigations Into Tesla Autopilot
feed.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched two formal defect investigations into Tesla's Autopilot system after multiple incidents where Teslas using the system collided with first-responder vehicles, including a fatal crash. This increased scrutiny could lead to recalls, tarnish Tesla's reputation, and highlights growing tensions between the company and regulators regarding the safety of its driver-assistance technologies. Critics argue that Tesla's approach is riskier compared to other automakers and that the current regulatory landscape in the U.S. has allowed for a "Wild West" environment for such technologies.

feed.title: The Pioneer of the Modern Workday Overhauls Its Schedule Once Again
feed.summary: Ford Motor Company has introduced a significant overhaul to its work schedule for 25,000 salaried employees, moving to a hybrid model where teams decide when to work from the office for collaboration and from home for individual tasks. This change, which is supported by internal research indicating a strong preference for hybrid work, follows in the footsteps of Henry Ford's original five-day, eight-hour work week. To facilitate this new approach, Ford has converted a third of its southeast Michigan workplaces into "collaboration centers" featuring advanced technology, amenities, and wellbeing spaces.

feed.title: Why the Immense Selling Pressure on the SPY ETF Must End
feed.summary: The article discusses why the intense selling pressure on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is likely to subside, presenting a buying opportunity. It attributes recent declines to concerns surrounding major holdings like Microsoft, Amazon, and Tesla, including antitrust reviews, Rivian losses, and Elon Musk's distraction with Twitter. Despite these issues, the author argues that the fundamental strength of the top companies in the S&P 500 remains, and investors should accumulate SPY shares on dips.

feed.title: What Is a VinFast EV?
feed.summary: VinFast, the automotive arm of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup, is entering the U.S. market with electric SUVs. The company plans to sell the VF 8 and VF 9 models, offering a unique battery subscription program and leveraging experienced global automotive talent and suppliers like Pininfarina. While promising, the venture carries risks for early adopters due to its newness and unproven nature, but its strong backing and clear timelines suggest a serious entry into the global automotive stage.

feed.title: CEO Steers Electric Truck Startup Rivian Through Supply Chain Twilight Zone
feed.summary: Rivian Automotive Inc. CEO R.J. Scaringe is struggling to ramp up electric vehicle production due to semiconductor supply chain issues, with chip suppliers prioritizing established customers over new entrants. The company's stock has plummeted, and it faces pressure from rising raw material costs and skepticism from competitors. Scaringe is actively working to reassure suppliers and aims to secure long-term funding for future expansion plans including a new plant and battery production.

feed.title: 7 of the Top EV Stocks from the DRIV ETF
feed.summary: This article identifies seven top EV stocks from the Global X Autonomous & Electric Vehicles ETF (DRIV), highlighting companies beyond traditional car manufacturers that contribute to the electric vehicle ecosystem. It covers prominent EV makers like Tesla, General Motors, and Ford, alongside technology and material innovators such as Honeywell, Nvidia, Qualcomm, and Apple. The piece emphasizes the broad growth potential in the EV sector, projecting a significant increase in EV adoption and the resulting opportunities for diverse companies involved in its expansion.

feed.title: RCD Is a Way to Spread Consumer Discretionary Bets
feed.summary: The article discusses the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF (RCD) as an alternative for investors seeking broader diversification in the consumer discretionary sector. It highlights how cap-weighted funds in this sector are heavily dominated by Amazon and Tesla, distorting their growth and value profiles. RCD, with its equal-weighting approach, offers a more balanced exposure, benefiting from recoveries in sub-groups like automotive, homebuilders, and travel and leisure.

feed.title: Tesla vehicles can no longer be bought at the end of their lease
feed.summary: Tesla has updated its policy, stating that vehicles delivered on or after April 15, 2022, are no longer eligible for purchase at the end of their lease. This decision comes amidst skyrocketing used-car prices and a history of Tesla occasionally withholding lease-end purchase options, particularly for the Model 3 for its intended "robotaxi" network. The change means third-party dealerships and individuals also cannot purchase leased Teslas, which may be influenced by the ongoing surge in both new and used EV prices.

feed.title: $202 million graphite processing plant breaks ground in Coosa County
feed.summary: Westwater Resources and Alabama Graphite Products broke ground on a $202 million graphite processing plant in Coosa County, Alabama. This plant, the first of its kind in the U.S., will produce battery-grade graphite crucial for electric vehicle batteries and is expected to create 100 jobs. The project aims to reduce U.S. reliance on imported graphite, particularly from China, and use a more environmentally friendly processing method.

feed.title: Pacific Gas and Electric commissions 182.5 MW Tesla battery energy storage system for substation
feed.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) has commissioned its 182.5 MW Elkhorn Battery system, a Tesla Megapack battery energy storage system (BESS), in Monterey County, California. This system, located at the Moss Landing electric substation, is now one of the largest lithium-ion systems globally, capable of storing and dispatching up to 730 MW hours of energy. The project aims to enhance electric system reliability, integrate renewable energy resources, and support California's clean energy future.

feed.title: Netflix shares fall more than 35% after streamer loses over 200,000 subscribers
feed.summary: Netflix shares plummeted over 35% after the company announced a loss of more than 200,000 subscribers in Q1 2022 and projected a further 2 million loss. This significant drop, wiping $50bn off its value, is attributed to increased competition, market saturation post-pandemic, inflation, and account sharing. Netflix plans to address this by tackling account sharing, improving programming quality, and considering an advertiser-supported subscription tier.

feed.title: Tesla profits surge as EV maker races past rising material costs
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. surpassed Wall Street estimates for quarterly revenue and profit, driven by price increases that offset rising material costs and a factory shutdown in Shanghai. Despite global supply chain issues and chip shortages, the EV maker saw its shares rise and revenue hit $18.8 billion in the first quarter of 2022, up 81 percent from the previous year. New factories in Berlin and Texas are expected to help meet demand and reduce reliance on its China factory.

feed.title: New 'black gold' of Alabama to put state on map for automakers |…
feed.summary: Alabama is set to become a major player in the automotive industry due to the discovery of a significant graphite deposit in the state, dubbed "black gold." Westwater Resources, Inc. and Alabama Graphite are building the first graphite processing plant of its kind in the US, which will produce refined graphite for lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles. This development positions Alabama to reduce foreign dependence on graphite and become a global leader in the EV supply chain.

feed.title: Elon Musk's Tesla Races Ahead of Rising Costs With Price Hikes
feed.summary: Tesla's Q1 results surged past Wall Street expectations, with higher prices helping the company overcome supply chain issues and rising costs. CEO Elon Musk indicated Tesla has a reasonable shot at achieving 60% vehicle delivery growth this year and that price increases effectively cover cost inflation. The strong performance also triggers $23 billion in new payouts for Musk, as the company navigates production challenges with its new factories and supply chain constraints.

feed.title: George Soros Losing $1.3 Billion on Electric Vehicles
feed.summary: Billionaire investor George Soros is reportedly facing significant losses, approximately $1.3 billion, on his massive investment in electric vehicle manufacturer Rivian Automotive. Despite Soros Fund Management's over $2 billion investment making Rivian nearly one-third of its total assets, the company's stock has plummeted due to production issues, supply chain problems, and rising costs. The article suggests Soros may leverage his political influence and philanthropic network to create a favorable policy environment for Rivian, given his history of using such power to influence markets.

feed.title: NEW: Groundbreaking takes place for $202M graphite processing plant
feed.summary: A $202 million graphite processing plant has broken ground in Coosa County, Alabama, marking the first facility of its kind in the US. This plant, operated by Westwater Resources and Alabama Graphite Products LLC, will produce battery-grade graphite essential for electric vehicle batteries, aiming to localize EV production. The project is expected to create 100 jobs and reduce the nation's reliance on imported graphite, bolstering Alabama's role in the growing EV sector.

feed.title: Self-driving Cars, Rare Earth Metals, ESG Activism: New ETFs On Syfe
feed.summary: Syfe has introduced three new ETFs to its platform: IDRV (iShares Self-Driving EV and Tech ETF), REMX (VanEck Rare Earth/Strategic Metals ETF), and VOTE (Engine No. 1 Transform 500 ETF). These ETFs offer investors exposure to rapidly growing sectors such as electric vehicles and autonomous driving, critical rare earth metals, and shareholder activism focused on ESG initiatives. The article details the holdings, market outlook, and expense ratios for each of these new investment options.

feed.title: Here's Why Elon Musk May Start Mining His Own Lithium
feed.summary: Elon Musk is calling for increased investment in lithium mining due to a significant supply-demand gap fueled by the rise of electric vehicles. Facing skyrocketing prices and a concentrated global supply, the Tesla chief suggested the company might begin mining its own lithium, a plan he first hinted at two years ago. The slow growth in lithium supply is attributed to a lack of investment following previous boom-bust cycles and the reliance on traditional mining countries, as newer, greener technologies have yet to reach commercial scale.

feed.title: Roundhill Cannabis ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:WEED) $WEED
feed.summary: The Roundhill Cannabis ETF (BATS:WEED) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in global cannabis and hemp companies. Launched on April 20, 2022, the ETF has $9.73 million in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.00%. The article provides details on the ETF's holdings, price performance, key statistics, and recent news headlines.

feed.title: Tesla Insurance Adds 3 More States, Plans to be Nationwide This Year
feed.summary: Tesla is expanding its insurance product to Colorado, Oregon, and Virginia, with plans to be nationwide by the end of the year. The company bases its rates on a driver's "Safety Score" calculated by in-car computers, aiming to save average drivers around 30 percent compared to competitors. Tesla Insurance aims to streamline the claims process through its app and help recover deductibles for not-at-fault accidents.

feed.title: Ferrari looking for partnerships, not mergers: CEO Vigna
feed.summary: Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna stated the company is interested in expanding its network through partnerships rather than mergers, asserting that Ferrari is essentially a luxury brand, not just a car brand. He dismissed rumors of an integration with Armani Group while highlighting recent partnerships with companies like Qualcomm to advance technology, especially towards batteries and digital transformation. Vigna also identified continental China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan as key growth markets for the luxury automaker.

feed.title: RBC and CIBC join banking group helping to finance Elon Musk’s bid for Twitter
feed.summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have committed US$1.15-billion to finance Elon Musk's US$44-billion takeover of Twitter Inc. The Canadian banks are participating in the lowest-risk part of the financing, a US$12.5-billion loan secured by a portion of Musk's Tesla shares. This indicates their involvement in the major acquisition while taking on the least financial risk among the lenders.

feed.title: GM asks suppliers to sign carbon neutrality pledge
feed.summary: General Motors is inviting its suppliers to sign an ESG Supplier Pledge, which is based on defined environmental, social, and governance factors. This move is part of GM's broader initiative to encourage carbon neutrality throughout its supply chain. The article was published on April 25, 2022.

feed.title: An entertainment company is using Twitter Spaces for its next earnings call—with 'Litquidity' as the moderator
feed.summary: RCI Hospitality Holdings, Inc., led by CEO Eric Langan, plans to host its upcoming earnings call on Twitter Spaces, aiming to reach a younger demographic and retail investors. This initiative, moderated by "Litquidity," is believed to be a first for earnings calls on the platform. The company believes this new format will increase engagement and visibility for its financial results.

feed.title: Twitter kicks off deal negotiations with Tesla boss Musk: Report
feed.summary: Twitter Inc. has begun deal negotiations with Elon Musk following his $43 billion acquisition offer, which he supported with financing details to woo shareholders. While the decision to engage does not guarantee acceptance of his $54.20 per share bid, it indicates Twitter is exploring the possibility of a sale on attractive terms. The social media company is also scrutinizing potential regulatory investigations into Musk and discussing concerns about a "poison pill" defense and a possible tender offer.

feed.title: Tax Breaks Cushion Tesla’s Texas Landing
feed.summary: Tesla received approximately $64 million in state and local tax breaks to build its Giga Texas factory in Austin, sparking debate over the efficacy of such incentives in generating promised economic benefits and jobs. The article highlights concerns that communities often give up more than they gain from these deals, drawing parallels to Tesla's Buffalo factory where job creation targets were not met. Community groups and local residents have raised issues regarding the deal's lack of oversight, potential for wage theft and unsafe conditions, and the challenge of local hiring due to language barriers, leading some local lawmakers to question the wisdom of future incentive deals.

feed.title: Lucid says Saudi Arabia will purchase up to 100,000 vehicles over 10 years
feed.summary: Electric carmaker Lucid Group Inc has signed an agreement with Saudi Arabia to supply up to 100,000 vehicles over ten years. The deal includes a commitment for 50,000 vehicles and an option for an additional 50,000, with deliveries starting no later than 2023. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is Lucid's largest shareholder, and Lucid plans to build an overseas production factory in Saudi Arabia.

feed.title: Can Elon Musk Run Tesla, Twitter and SpaceX? We’ll Soon Find Out.
feed.summary: Elon Musk's ability to simultaneously lead Tesla, Twitter, and SpaceX is being questioned as he takes on another major project with the Twitter acquisition. Despite previously lamenting his lack of time, Musk has a track record of successfully juggling multiple ventures, including achieving a record profit at Tesla, securing financing for Twitter, and promoting his other companies. The article sets the stage for observing how he manages these demanding roles.

feed.title: Does a Musk-owned Twitter dim Tesla’s star?
feed.summary: Elon Musk's bid to buy Twitter has raised concerns about its potential impact on Tesla's reputation and future. Observers question whether this acquisition distracts Musk from Tesla's core mission and if the controversies surrounding Twitter could negatively affect the automaker's brand and stock performance. While some see potential for new alliances and free speech advocacy, others worry about conflicts of interest and potential harm to customer perception and privacy.

feed.title: Invesco launches ETF focused on metals required for electric vehicles, energy transition
feed.summary: Invesco has launched a new exchange-traded fund (ETF) called the Invesco Electric Vehicle Metals Commodity Strategy No K-1 ETF (EVMT), which focuses on metals critical for electric vehicles and the energy transition. The fund holds futures contracts for aluminum, copper, nickel, cobalt, zinc, and iron ore, excluding lithium due to liquidity concerns. This launch comes amid soaring metals prices and growing demand as the EV market expands, with Invesco betting on continued volatility and growth in the sector.

feed.title: Musk loses bid to end SEC agreement on oversight of Tesla tweets
feed.summary: A U.S. judge rejected Elon Musk's attempt to end a 2018 settlement with the SEC that requires oversight of his Tesla tweets. The agreement stemmed from a 2018 tweet about taking Tesla private and also entails a separate SEC investigation into Musk's tweets about selling Tesla stock. The judge stated that Musk cannot retract an agreement he knowingly entered.

feed.title: Ford lost $3.1 billion in the first quarter. (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Ford Motor reported a $3.1 billion loss in the first quarter of 2022, primarily due to a significant decline in the value of its investment in electric vehicle start-up Rivian. The company also faced challenges from the ongoing global chip shortage, which limited vehicle production despite strong demand for its trucks and SUVs. Ford, however, maintained its full-year profit outlook, banking on improved semiconductor supply and rapid growth in electric vehicle sales.

feed.title: Judge rules for Elon Musk in $13 bln lawsuit over Tesla-SolarCity deal
feed.summary: A Delaware judge has ruled in favor of Elon Musk in a lawsuit alleging that he unjustly enriched himself through Tesla's 2016 acquisition of SolarCity. Tesla shareholders had sought up to $13 billion in damages, claiming Musk coerced the board into buying the struggling solar panel maker. The court found that Tesla paid a fair price for SolarCity, and the acquisition was beneficial to the company.

feed.title: What Elon Musk’s Twitter Takeover Means for Trump’s TRUTH Social
feed.summary: Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter has sparked debate about its implications for former President Donald Trump's TRUTH Social. While some conservatives on Twitter celebrated the deal and anticipate the return of suspended accounts, Trump has stated he will not rejoin Twitter, opting instead to focus on TRUTH Social. The deal initially led to a surge in TRUTH Social downloads but also introduced uncertainty about its long-term growth and financial stability due to renewed interest in Twitter and the complexities of its SPAC merger.

feed.title: Tesla Inc: Report on policies and practices to reduce climate-related water risk
feed.summary: This report details a shareholder resolution requesting Tesla Inc. to assess and report its ongoing climate-related water risk exposure and mitigation policies. It highlights Tesla's operations in water-stressed regions and criticisms regarding the water usage of its factories in Berlin-Brandenburg and Austin. The resolution calls for greater transparency, including facility-specific water data, risk assessments, and integration of water management into governance.

feed.title: How to Invest in Lithium in Latin America
feed.summary: This article explores investment opportunities in the lithium industry, particularly in Latin America, where 50% of the world’s lithium reserves are located across Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile. It discusses investing through ETFs like Lithium & Battery Tech (LIT) and individual company shares such as Albemarle (ALB), Tesla (TSLA), TDK, Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile SA (SQM), and Posco, highlighting their performance and market trends. The piece also delves into the complexities of the lithium market, the impact of electric vehicle demand, and future price sustainability.

feed.title: RBC, CIBC to lend Elon Musk $1.5 billion for Twitter takeover
feed.summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have pledged a combined $1.5 billion to help finance Elon Musk's $56-billion bid to acquire Twitter. This contribution is part of a larger $32.5 billion financing package from 12 banks, with RBC providing $956.5 million and CIBC contributing $510 million. The article also touches on other recent financing deals, including increased investment by The Home Depot Canada Foundation for youth homelessness, funding for QuadFi to offer personal loans to underserved groups, and Mavrck's acquisition of Later.

feed.title: Boom to gloom: Cathie Wood’s Ark headed for its worst-ever month
authors: Thyagaraju Adinarayan and Sam Potter and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Cathie Wood's flagship ARK Innovation fund is set for its worst-ever month, with a 26% decline in April, bringing its total drop to nearly 70% from its 2021 peak. This downturn reflects a significant shift from its pandemic-era success, as key holdings like Zoom and Teladoc Health have tumbled. Despite the poor performance, Wood maintains confidence in her long-term strategy and top holdings, even as the fund's outperformance against the S&P 500 has diminished.

feed.title: Tesla’s Ambitions in India Will Test Elon Musk’s Commitment to ‘Free Speech’
feed.summary: Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter could provide the Indian government with leverage to curb critics due to Tesla's business aspirations in the country. Tesla is currently lobbying the Modi government for reduced import taxes, creating a potential conflict of interest between Musk's stated commitment to free speech on Twitter and his business goals. Critics worry this could lead to increased online suppression of dissent, particularly affecting marginalized groups in India.

feed.title: Musk sells Tesla shares worth $8.5 billion ahead of Twitter takeover
feed.summary: Elon Musk sold $8.5 billion worth of Tesla shares to help finance his $44 billion acquisition of Twitter. He stated on Twitter that no further Tesla sales are planned after this. This sale follows Musk's earlier offloading of Tesla stock in late 2021 after polling Twitter users.

feed.title: Cyber Risk for Vehicles
feed.summary: This article discusses the increasing cyber risks associated with the fast-paced evolution of vehicle automation and internet-connected technologies. It categorizes intelligent vehicles and outlines the emerging risks related to privacy, security, and safety, highlighting vulnerabilities in vehicle software. The article also touches upon the implications for motor insurance, distinguishing between tangible property loss and pure financial loss exposures.

feed.title: Detroit automakers aren't letting up on a long-standing rivalry, even as they pivot to take on Tesla
feed.summary: The historic rivalry between General Motors, Ford, and Stellantis remains strong, even as they all pivot to develop electric vehicles to compete with Tesla. This rivalry was evident when GM and Stellantis attempted to overshadow Ford's F-150 Lightning launch with their own EV announcements, a common practice in the "bloodthirsty" automotive industry that ultimately benefits consumers through innovation. Despite the focus on each other, analysts suggest the Detroit automakers need to prioritize competing with newcomers like Tesla to avoid repeating past mistakes.

feed.title: US plug-in vehicle sales hit a record high in Q1, led by Tesla and California
feed.summary: US plug-in vehicle sales reached a record high in Q1, driven significantly by Tesla and California. Nationally, approximately 208,000 electric vehicles were sold, with California accounting for about 40% of these sales. Tesla maintained a substantial lead, especially in California, where its Model 3 and Model Y topped sales charts.

feed.title: Steer Into the Future with Delphi Technologies by Your Side
feed.summary: Delphi Technologies highlights its extensive range of steering and suspension products, emphasizing their quality, rigorous testing, and suitability for next-generation vehicles like EVs. The company provides premium replacement parts that meet or exceed OE specifications, addressing challenges such as increased battery weight in electric vehicles with lightweight solutions. Delphi Technologies also offers robust technical support and training for automotive professionals.

feed.title: Tesla Stock Gets Preview From NIO, Other Chinese EV Makers. It Wasn't Good.
feed.summary: Chinese electric vehicle makers NIO, XPeng, and Li Auto reported disappointing April delivery numbers due to COVID-19 related production shutdowns in China. This news serves as a concerning precursor for Tesla investors, suggesting potential similar impacts on Tesla's own delivery figures. The Covid outbreak is significantly affecting EV output in the region.

feed.title: News | Of HBO’s The Gilded Age, Elon Musk, and the Legacy of Jay Gould
feed.summary: The article draws parallels between historical figure Jay Gould, contemporary businessman Elon Musk, and the HBO series "The Gilded Age." It highlights common traits such as being self-made, workaholics, and using wealth as a tool for power, while also noting differences like Gould's disinterest in societal acceptance. The author, Ed Renehan, whose biography of Gould was a primary source for the HBO series, discusses how both historical and modern innovators often face public vilification.

feed.title: China’s COVID hard line eats into everything from Teslas to tacos
feed.summary: China's strict 'zero COVID' policies have severely impacted various industries, from luxury goods to fast-food restaurants, causing significant lost sales and shaken consumer confidence. Lockdowns, particularly in Shanghai, have disrupted supply chains and drastically reduced demand for products like electric vehicles, with analysts warning of a growing risk of recession. While some cities are offering incentives to boost spending, the prolonged impact of pandemic controls continues to threaten the consumer sector across China.

feed.title: The Politics of Lithium in Mexico: Much Ado About Nothing?
feed.summary: Bradford Cooke, Founder and CEO of Endeavour Silver Corp, questions Mexico's decision to nationalize lithium mining, arguing that the country lacks the necessary expertise, technology, and capital. He highlights that lithium is abundant globally, and current state-only models in other countries like Bolivia have resulted in low production despite large reserves. Cooke suggests that restricting private enterprise in lithium mining might be an unproductive move for Mexico.

feed.title: (Crypto) Action! Indie Movie Studio Received $10M in Bitcoin for Shares in October
feed.summary: Angel Studios, a Utah-based movie studio, raised $10.6 million in Bitcoin during a stock sale in October 2021, according to SEC filings. This unique transaction involved venture capital firms Uncorrelated Ventures and Gigafund, with the latter having ties to Elon Musk. Despite the successful crypto fundraise, Angel Studios reported a $2.7 million impairment loss on its Bitcoin holdings by the end of 2021.

feed.title: Inside Out: EV’s KARS ETF, TSLA, And NIO
feed.summary: Anthony Sassine discussed strong electric vehicle sales in 2022 on TD Ameritrade Network, highlighting the impact of the Russia/Ukraine war on the EV supply chain. He mentioned the KraneShares Electric Vehicles & Future Mobility ETF (KARS), which includes companies like Tesla (TSLA), Analog Devices (ADI), Ford (F), and Mercedes-Benz (DDAIF). The article projects significant growth for the EV market, with global market value expected to reach $1.4 trillion by 2027.

feed.title: Elon Musk Secures $7.14B in New Financing for Twitter Deal, Holds Talks to Keep Jack Dorsey on Board as Investor
feed.summary: Elon Musk has secured nearly $7.14 billion in new financing commitments for his acquisition of Twitter, bringing in investors such as Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and Saudi Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Alsaud. The new financing reduces Musk's margin loan for the deal. Additionally, Musk is in discussions with existing Twitter shareholders, including co-founder Jack Dorsey, about potentially retaining their equity in the company post-buyout instead of receiving cash.

feed.title: Navigating America’s net-zero frontier: A guide for business leaders
feed.summary: This article provides a guide for US business leaders on navigating America's net-zero transition by 2050, outlining a pathway that could create $27 trillion in capital spending opportunities. It identifies five high-potential climate solutions—renewable power, electrification, operational efficiency, clean fuels, and carbon capture—and discusses macro trends like accelerated technology deployment and significant capital requirements. The authors encourage companies to proactively assess business risks and opportunities, suggesting strategies for value creation including portfolio transformation and green business building to thrive in a net-zero economy.

feed.title: Elon Musk Secures $7.1 Billion in New Financing for Twitter
feed.summary: Elon Musk has secured approximately $7.1 billion in new financing commitments for his $44 billion acquisition of Twitter Inc. The funding comes from various investors, including Binance, Brookfield, Fidelity Management & Research, and Qatar Holding. This new financing reduces the margin loan associated with the deal and Musk is also in discussions with Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey about contributing shares.

feed.title: Brookfield's venture capital arm cuts biggest check yet for Elon Musk's Twitter buyout
feed.summary: Brookfield Asset Management's venture capital division, Brookfield Growth, has committed US$250 million to Elon Musk's US$7.1 billion equity raise for his acquisition of Twitter Inc. This investment marks the largest single check written by Brookfield Growth to date and stems from an existing relationship between the billionaire and the Canadian asset manager. The partnership also extends to other ventures, including a sustainable housing development in Austin, Texas, involving Musk's Boring Co. and Tesla Energy.

feed.title: The Landscape for Digital Asset Custodial Services in 2022
feed.summary: This article discusses the evolving landscape of digital asset custodial services in 2022, highlighting the significant growth of digital assets and the security challenges they present. It explains the need for specialized custody due to the unique nature of cryptocurrencies, contrasting it with traditional asset custody. The piece also outlines various storage mechanisms, client needs, regulatory considerations, and different custody options available to investors and financial institutions.

feed.title: Stock Price Trading Dynamics and Splits
feed.summary: This article examines the impact of stock price on market quality features and the decision to split a stock, focusing on the recent trend of large corporations splitting their high-priced stocks. It analyzes various market features like consolidated quoted spreads, quoted size coverage, and quote volatility across different stock price and volume categories. The analysis suggests that targeting stock prices in the $50-$100 range for liquid securities offers the best market quality results, although the evidence for splitting less liquid stocks is less convincing.

feed.title: ICON Announces Tom vonReichbauer as Chief Financial Officer
feed.summary: ICON has announced that Tom vonReichbauer, a veteran leader from companies like Tesla, Nest, Google, and Sunrun, will join as its Chief Financial Officer on June 1, 2022. vonReichbauer brings extensive experience in disruptive technologies and financial leadership, aligning with ICON's mission to transform construction through large-scale 3D printing. His appointment is expected to help ICON scale its solutions for housing challenges and continue its work in providing resilient, dignified housing and developing off-world construction systems.

feed.title: Report: Tesla adds swiveling screen to yoke-equipped Model S
feed.summary: Tesla's Model S is reportedly shipping with a new swiveling central touchscreen, despite no official confirmation from the company. Owner reports and photos from a Tesla store in Taiwan show the screen can be tilted towards the driver, and a video demonstrates a motorized pivot. This update follows a significant interior refresh for the Model S and X, which included a steering yoke, and comes amidst increasing competition in advanced screen technology from other luxury EV manufacturers like Lucid and BMW.

feed.title: AEB Market to Grow by 2.1x by 2032
feed.summary: The automatic emergency braking (AEB) market is projected to grow at an eight percent CAGR, exceeding $63,591.7 million by 2032, according to a Future Market Insights study. This growth is driven by stricter government regulations on car safety, increasing driver safety concerns, and higher expenditure on ADAS. East Asia's growing passenger-vehicle fleet will significantly fuel regional AEB market growth, expected to rise at a CAGR of 10.2 percent during the forecast period.

feed.title: Tesla will pay travel costs for staff seeking abortion services
feed.summary: Tesla announced it will cover travel and lodging costs for employees who need to seek healthcare services, including abortions, unavailable in their home state. This move comes as several states, including Texas where Tesla moved its headquarters, have implemented stricter abortion laws. Other companies have adopted similar policies in response to the changing legal landscape surrounding abortion access.

feed.title: Brazil's Vale signs long-term deal to supply Tesla with nickel
feed.summary: Brazilian mining company Vale SA has signed a long-term deal to supply Tesla Inc with low-carbon Class 1 nickel from its Canadian operations. This agreement aligns with Vale's strategy to increase its exposure to the electric vehicle industry, aiming for 30% to 40% of its Class 1 nickel sales to go to this fast-growing sector. The nickel supplied will come from Vale's Long Harbour plant in Newfoundland and Labrador, which produces nickel rounds with a low carbon footprint.

feed.title: 3 Surefire Stocks That Can Turn $200,000 Into $1 Million by 2030
feed.summary: This article identifies three stocks — Nio, Upstart Holdings, and Pinterest — that have the potential to turn a $200,000 investment into $1 million by 2030, despite recent market downturns. The author emphasizes that while the stock market has experienced corrections, these companies possess strong catalysts and innovative business models that position them for significant long-term growth. The piece details how each company, through unique offerings and market positioning, is poised for substantial returns within the next eight years.

feed.title: Tesla’s 10-Word Rule Every Employee Has to Follow Is Simply Brilliant
feed.summary: This article discusses Tesla's "do the right thing" aspiration as outlined in its 2021 Impact Report, highlighting how this simple 10-word phrase serves as a core principle for all employees. It explains that this aspiration encourages self-awareness within the company, guiding decisions related to hiring, customer interaction, and overall leadership. The author emphasizes that this principle helps define the company's direction and sets clear expectations for every team member.

feed.title: Time might be right to take ride in convertibles
feed.summary: Tracy Maitland suggests that convertible bonds offer institutional investors a valuable way to diversify their fixed-income portfolios, especially given the current low returns from core strategies. The article highlights the potential of convertibles as a strategic asset in challenging market conditions.

feed.title: When Momentum Fails
feed.summary: The article discusses how momentum, a historically strong investment factor, has shown signs of faltering in recent months despite its long-term outperformance. It highlights that while momentum stocks have often delivered strong returns, periods of market decline and shifts in investor sentiment can lead to sharp drawdowns, emphasizing that nothing lasts forever in investing.

feed.title: Elon Musk says Tesla open to buying a mining company
feed.summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, has indicated the company is open to acquiring a mining company to secure its own supply of electric vehicle (EV) metals. This consideration stems from growing concerns about potential shortages of critical metals like lithium, nickel, and copper needed for EV production later this decade. Tesla aims to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy and views direct mining involvement as a possibility if it helps overcome supply limitations, despite having no prior experience in mining operations.

feed.title: Honda Rolls Out Free Maintenance Plan for 2023 Models
feed.summary: Honda is introducing "Honda Service Pass," a complimentary maintenance plan for its 2023 models, providing basic services for the first two years or 24,000 miles. The 2023 Honda Odyssey will be the first vehicle to include this plan, featuring a new Sport trim and starting at $38,635. This initiative aims to help new Honda owners manage rising vehicle ownership costs.

feed.title: Tesla halts production in Shanghai over supply issues: Report
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. halted production at its Shanghai plant on Monday due to persistent supply chain issues, just three weeks after partially resuming operations following a COVID-19 lockdown. The suspension highlights the complexities of maintaining manufacturing in China amidst its battle against the coronavirus and strict lockdown measures. It remains uncertain when production will restart, impacting Tesla's goals to increase output and reflecting broader auto industry disruptions in China.

feed.title: TI Touts Solid-state Relays to Enable Safer EVs
feed.summary: Texas Instruments (TI) has introduced two new solid-state relay ICs, the TPSI3050-Q1 and TPSI2140-Q1, designed to enhance safety and reliability in electric vehicles, especially as battery architectures shift from 400V to 800V. These devices aim to replace traditional mechanical relays by offering longer operating life, higher isolation capabilities, and reduced solution size. The solid-state relays integrate power and signal isolation on a single chip, providing faster switching speeds crucial for critical EV safety functions.

feed.title: Tesla recalls 130,000 EVs for touch screen malfunctions
feed.summary: Tesla is recalling approximately 130,000 electric vehicles in the US due to touch screens that can overheat and go blank, affecting certain Model S, Model X, Model 3, and Model Y vehicles. The issue stems from insufficient cooling of central processing units during fast charging, which can lead to slow screens or blank displays, potentially increasing crash risk. Tesla is addressing the problem with online software updates to improve temperature management, having already initiated updates on May 3.

feed.title: Musk says he will stay at Tesla as long as he is useful
feed.summary: Elon Musk stated he would remain CEO of Tesla Inc. as long as he is useful, addressing investor concerns that his acquisition of Twitter would divert his attention. He also downplayed the impact of China's COVID-19 lockdowns on Tesla's Shanghai factory, noting the country's restrictions were lifting rapidly. Musk further indicated that Tesla has no immediate plans for additional factories in China but will expand its existing Shanghai facility.

feed.title: Musk: Tesla Could Buy Mining Company
feed.summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla is open to acquiring a mining company if it becomes necessary to accelerate the global transition to sustainable energy. This announcement comes as the electric vehicle industry faces concerns about a shortage of critical metals like lithium, copper, and nickel needed for EV batteries. Tesla aims to produce 20 million vehicles annually by 2030, a significant jump from the one million produced in 2021.

feed.title: Red Hat Linux to drive General Motors' Ultifi vehicle operating system
feed.summary: Red Hat will supply General Motors with its In-Vehicle Operating System (IVOS) to serve as a Linux base for GM's Ultifi software platform. This partnership aims to enable "software-defined vehicles" that will generate new revenue streams through continuous updates and new features. The Red Hat IVOS is expected to gain ISO 26262 certification in 2023, ensuring it meets the high safety standards required for in-vehicle electronic systems.

feed.title: Mining is key to the energy transition, but it's still unloved
feed.summary: The mining sector is crucial for the global energy transition and achieving net-zero emissions, yet it remains largely undervalued and faces significant challenges. Despite the pressing demand for critical minerals like copper, lithium, and nickel, the industry struggles to attract investment, streamline government approvals, and overcome its negative public image. Experts emphasize the urgent need for a shift in perception and policy to prevent raw material shortages that could hinder the energy transition.

feed.title: Tesla recalls cars for overheating issue—of screens, not battery packs
feed.summary: Tesla is recalling 129,960 vehicles, including 2021-2022 Model S and Model X, and 2022 Model 3 and Model Y, due to an overheating infotainment CPU during fast charging. This issue can cause screen lag or restarts, and is considered a safety concern because of the rearview camera feed. Tesla plans to address this with an over-the-air software update.

feed.title: U.S. judge says Musk recklessly tweeted that 'funding secured' for taking Tesla private
feed.summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that Elon Musk's 2018 tweets claiming "funding secured" to take Tesla private were inaccurate and reckless, as there was no concrete financing from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund at the time. This pre-trial decision marks a significant win for investors suing Musk for allegedly inflating Tesla's stock prices with false statements. The ruling determines Musk knowingly made false statements, leaving the determination of damages to shareholders for an upcoming jury trial.

feed.title: Netflix and TikTok Cultures Reveal the Dark Side of Innovation
feed.summary: This article explores the demanding work cultures at highly innovative companies like Netflix and TikTok, highlighting the "dark side of innovation." It discusses how the relentless pursuit of growth and excellence leads to long hours, poor work-life balance, and employee burnout, despite the prestige and career opportunities offered. The article contrasts the inspiring public image of innovation with the personal costs borne by employees in these fast-paced environments.

feed.title: Exclusive: Tesla puts India entry plan on hold after deadlock on tariffs
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. has temporarily halted its plans to sell electric cars in India due to a persistent disagreement with the Indian government over import tariffs. The company had failed to secure lower import taxes for its vehicles, prompting it to abandon its search for showroom space and reassign some of its India team members. The Indian government insists on local manufacturing commitment before it will reduce tariffs.

feed.title: Electric Tractors Tackle Off-Highway Jobs
feed.summary: The agricultural and construction industries are seeing a shift from traditional diesel engines to electric drivetrains for tractors and other off-highway equipment. This transition is driven by changing emission standards, the benefits of quieter operation, and instant torque. Major manufacturers like John Deere, CNH Industrial, and Volvo Construction Equipment, alongside startups like Monarch Tractor and Solectrac, are investing heavily in developing battery-powered machinery, leveraging EV technologies from the automotive industry.

feed.title: Bill Gates Sells $940 Million of CN Rail Stock
feed.summary: Bill Gates' investment firm, Cascade Investment, sold approximately $940 million worth of Canadian National Railway Co. shares between April 27 and May 12, reducing its stake in the company to about 9%. This sale is part of an ongoing reduction in ownership since May 2021. Gates' former wife, Melinda French Gates, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation also sold significant portions of their Canadian National shares.

feed.title: Tesla targets Silver Spring for new service center
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. is planning to open a new service center in Silver Spring, Maryland, expanding its presence in the Greater Washington area. The electric automaker will lease a single-story office building for this new facility. This move signifies Tesla's continued growth and investment in its service infrastructure.

feed.title: 10 Things You Need To Know About XPeng Motors
feed.summary: XPeng Motors, an EV startup founded in 2014, has rapidly grown, delivering 98,000 cars in 2021 with 263% year-on-year growth. Originally focusing on the Chinese market, the company is now expanding into Europe and potentially the US, offering a range of electric vehicles from SUVs like the G9 to sedans like the P7, many equipped with advanced self-driving technology. Despite facing significant competition, XPeng aims to become a major player in the global EV market.

feed.title: Here's How GM Plans to Knock Tesla Off Its Pedestal
feed.summary: General Motors (GM) aims to surpass Tesla in EV sales by mid-decade, with CEO Mary Barra stating GM will sell more EVs than any other manufacturer in the U.S. The strategy focuses on offering more affordable EV options, including the upcoming Equinox EV priced around $30,000, to compete with Tesla's higher price points. While Tesla currently dominates the market, GM and other legacy automakers are ramping up EV production to challenge its lead, especially with affordable trucks and SUVs.

feed.title: 꿈을 먹고 자란 주식 '하락'에 베팅했더니…연초 대비 96% 수익률
feed.summary: 미국 성장주에 집중 투자하는 '아크 이노베이션 ETF(ARKK)'의 올해 수익률이 연초 대비 57% 하락하면서, 이들 성장주의 하락에 베팅하는 상장지수펀드(ETF)들이 주목받고 있다. 특히, ARKK의 일일 등락폭을 기준으로 -1배 수익을 내도록 설계된 '터틀캐피탈 숏 이노베이션 ETF(SARK)'는 연초 대비 89% 상승했다. 스팩(SPAC) 합병을 통해 상장한 기업들을 추종하는 ETF의 하락에 베팅하는 '더 숏 디-스팩 ETF(SOGU)'도 연초 대비 96%의 수익률을 기록했다.

feed.title: Tesla delays plan to restore Shanghai output to pre-lockdown levels
feed.summary: Tesla has postponed its plan to restore production at its Shanghai plant to pre-lockdown levels by at least a week due to ongoing COVID-19 restrictions. The company now aims to increase daily output to 2,600 units from May 23, having maintained a single shift producing around 1,200 units daily for the current week. Challenges include difficulties doubling the workforce for "closed-loop" operations and uncertainties in supplier and logistics restoration.

feed.title: China regulator says Tesla recalling 107,293 China-made Model 3, Model Y vehicles
feed.summary: China's market regulatory agency has announced that Tesla is recalling 107,293 China-made Model 3 and Model Y vehicles. The recall is due to a potential overheating issue that can cause the center touchscreen display to malfunction. This overheating could also lead to other problems, including issues with windshield settings and gear displays.

feed.title: GM is betting its Ultium batteries will lead the automaker to EV dominance
feed.summary: General Motors is making a significant investment in electric vehicle technology, specifically with its new Ultium platform, to become a leader in the EV market. The Ultium platform, centered around uniquely designed batteries developed with LG Energy Solutions, aims to reduce cobalt usage by 70% and lower battery pack costs, making EVs more competitive. GM believes these innovations will enable them to dominate the North American EV market by 2025, challenging current leader Tesla.

feed.title: Why S&P booted Tesla from its ESG index
feed.summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Tesla from its S&P 500 ESG Index due to a decline in its ESG rank compared to global peers. Despite Tesla's role in the transition to electric vehicles, the decision was influenced by claims of racial discrimination, poor working conditions at its factory, and its handling of a federal investigation into autopilot-related deaths. Elon Musk called ESG an "outrageous scam" in response to the decision.

feed.title: Tesla dumped by S&P ESG index as Musk calls label a ‘scam’
feed.summary: Tesla has been removed from the S&P 500 ESG Index due to concerns regarding working conditions, its handling of investigations into driver-assistance system deaths, and a lack of low-carbon strategy and business conduct codes. While S&P Dow Jones Indices noted Tesla's ESG score remained "fairly stable," it slipped against improving global peers. CEO Elon Musk subsequently criticized ESG as a "scam" and "fundamentally flawed," stating it has been "weaponized by phony social justice warriors."

feed.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Target and growth stocks sink
feed.summary: Wall Street closed sharply lower on Wednesday after Target's stock plummeted by about a quarter of its value, exposing concerns about the U.S. economy due to surging prices. This marked the worst one-day loss for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average since June 2020, as inflation continued to erode consumer purchasing power, impacting retailers and prompting a market sell-off. Megacap growth stocks also contributed to the decline, with the Nasdaq falling significantly, amidst broader economic worries including rising inflation, supply chain issues, and central bank tightening.

feed.title: Innovation Meets Productivity at AGCO Jackson Campus
feed.summary: The article highlights the AGCO Jackson campus as a world-class manufacturing facility for agricultural machinery, emphasizing its focus on innovation, productivity, and a strong employee culture. It details why Jackson, Minnesota, was chosen for the plant, the importance of its workforce in agricultural production, and how the company is adapting to new challenges like supply chain issues and evolving market trends by prioritizing "farmer first" solutions and behavioral hiring.

feed.title: AC Hotels by Marriott developer buys land in St. Johns Town Center
feed.summary: OTO Development LLC, the developer behind the AC Hotels by Marriott project in St. Johns Town Center, has purchased 2.725 acres of land for $1.18 million. The four-story, 118-room hotel, costing an estimated $18 million, is scheduled to start construction in the first quarter of 2022 and be completed in the second quarter of 2023. This project is a joint venture between OTO and Simon Property Group, with OTO serving as the managing partner.

feed.title: Musk's ESG attack spotlights $35 trillion industry confusion
feed.summary: Elon Musk's criticism of ESG scores, particularly after Tesla was removed from S&P's ESG index, highlights growing confusion and disagreement within the $35 trillion sustainable investing industry. While some believe ESG should reward companies actively doing good for the environment and society, others, including rating agencies, view it as a tool to assess a company's risk exposure to ESG factors. This divergence in understanding means that companies contributing to climate change can still be included if they show efforts to mitigate ESG risks, contrasting with Musk's perspective that Tesla, despite its environmental contributions, was penalized for other issues like working conditions.

feed.title: 10 Most Valuable Car Companies On The Planet
feed.summary: This article lists the 10 most valuable car companies globally as of December 2022, highlighting the significant market shifts caused by companies like Tesla and Rivian. It details each company's origins, key brands, and market valuation, emphasizing the automotive industry's evolving landscape with the rise of electric vehicles. Tesla leads the list, underscoring the dramatic growth of innovative new entrants compared to traditional automakers.

feed.title: A superstar investor with the Midas touch or just lucky? The puzzle of Cathie Wood
feed.summary: Cathie Wood, CEO of ARK Invest, became a superstar investor during the pandemic with her ARK Innovation ETF returning 150% in 2020. However, her funds are struggling significantly in 2022, leading to questions about her investment strategy and whether her past success was due to skill or luck. Despite criticism and poor performance, Wood remains confident, advocating for a five-year investment horizon and continuing to attract new investor money.

feed.title: Rosenbluth Discusses ESG, Tesla, and More on Bloomberg
feed.summary: Todd Rosenbluth recently appeared on Bloomberg to discuss various ETF-related topics, including the growing appeal of low-cost bond ETFs over mutual funds, defensive and factor investing strategies, and specific ETF rebalances. He also addressed why Tesla was dropped from the S&P 500 ESG index, emphasizing the differentiation between environmental, social, and governance factors. Rosenbluth highlighted the importance of looking beyond labels for ESG ETFs, as they can differ significantly.

feed.title: Todd Rosenbluth Talks ESG, Tesla, and More on Bloomberg
feed.summary: Todd Rosenbluth discussed the shifts in bond fund flows, the rise of defensive and value investment strategies, and the complexities surrounding Tesla's exclusion from the S&P 500 ESG index during his appearance on Bloomberg. He highlighted the importance of understanding the different components ("e," "s," and "g") of ESG and how momentum ETFs rebalance. Rosenbluth also emphasized that investors need to look beyond labels, as not all ESG or factor-based ETFs are the same.

feed.title: Lithium Miner Albemarle Lifts Outlook as EV Battery Demand Surges
feed.summary: Albemarle Corp., the world’s largest lithium producer, has raised its financial outlook for the second time this month. This adjustment is due to strong demand for electric vehicle batteries and tight lithium supply, leading battery makers to pay higher prices for the metal. The company now projects sales between $5.8 billion and $6.2 billion for the current year.

feed.title: Airbnb Pulling Out of China Thanks to Stiff Competition From Super-Apps
feed.summary: Airbnb is discontinuing its short-term rental operations in China starting July 30, 2022, due to intense local competition from "super-apps" and strict COVID-19 lockdowns. While Chinese customers can still use Airbnb for international travel, the company will remove approximately 150,000 listings from its platform in China. This move follows other American companies like LinkedIn, Yahoo, Urban Outfitters, and Everlane that have also recently exited the Chinese market.

feed.title: Tesla plans a drive-in movie restaurant in Hollywood
feed.summary: Tesla has submitted documents to the city of Los Angeles for a 24-hour drive-in movie restaurant with a 28-stall Supercharger station in Hollywood, a concept Elon Musk has been teasing for four years. The plans detail a two-story diner with indoor and outdoor seating, two LED movie screens for drive-in viewing, and food delivery to cars. This futuristic establishment would replace a Shakey's Pizza and requires city approval before proceeding.

feed.title: Texas Is Now Home to More Fortune 500 Companies Than Any Other State, and I’m Not Surprised
feed.summary: Texas has become the leading state for Fortune 500 company headquarters, surpassing New York and California, with 53 businesses currently located there. This migration, including major companies like Tesla and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, is attributed to Texas's business-friendly policies, lower cost of living, attractive tax environment (no income tax), educated workforce, and robust infrastructure. The author, whose company U.S. Global Investors operates in Texas, expresses no surprise at this trend, highlighting the state's economic appeal.

feed.title: How a Sustainability Index Can Keep Exxon but Drop Tesla – And 3 Ways to Fix ESG Ratings to Meet Investors’ Expectations
feed.summary: A major stock index recently dropped Tesla but kept ExxonMobil, sparking debate over ESG ratings. Professor Tom Lyon explains that ESG ratings often compare companies within their industry, leading to situations where an oil giant ranks better than an EV manufacturer due to different criteria and internal factors like social and governance issues. He suggests improving ESG ratings by allowing investors to target specific objectives, breaking down ESG into individual "E," "S," and "G" metrics, and enhancing disclosure requirements.
feed.source: University of Michigan's Ross School of Business
feed.source_domain: University of Michigan's Ross School of Business

feed.title: Hyperion looks to slower growth for a helping hand
feed.summary: Australia's largest growth manager, Hyperion, is betting on a counterintuitive outcome—an economic downturn and anemic growth—to revive its performance. Despite a 36% year-to-date loss, Hyperion's CIO Mark Arnold believes that high inflation and high interest rates are temporary and will retreat as the economy cools, providing a tailwind for growth stocks. The firm argues that its disruptive holdings, like Tesla and Amazon, will outperform in a cooler economy where growth is scarce, forcing capital allocators to invest in companies with double-digit earnings growth.

feed.title: Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles revoked in California
feed.summary: The California Department of Motor Vehicles has revoked Pony.ai's permit to test autonomous vehicles with safety drivers due to the company's failure to monitor the driving records of its safety drivers. The DMV found numerous violations on the driving records of active Pony.ai safety drivers, emphasizing the critical role of clean driving records for safety drivers. Pony.ai, while stating pride in its safety record of over 6.8 million accident-free autonomous miles, had previously lost a permit for driverless testing after a collision and subsequently recalled vehicles due to software issues.

feed.title: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions, BYU–Hawaii complete campuswide renewable energy system
feed.summary: Duke Energy Sustainable Solutions and Brigham Young University–Hawaii have completed a campuswide renewable energy system, including solar and battery storage. This system is expected to meet 39% of the university's energy needs annually and save over $20 million in utility costs. The project aims to reduce the university's environmental impact and dependence on Hawaii's energy grid, utilizing a 20-year power purchase agreement to finance the initiative.

feed.title: 5 lessons I learned from helping to launch Tesla’s Model S
feed.summary: The article shares five business lessons learned by Sukemasa Kabayama, the former President of Tesla Japan, during the challenging five-week launch of the Model S in Japan in 2014. These lessons emphasize creativity, holistic customer experience, laser focus on outcomes, the principle of "less is more," and clarity in problem-solving. Kabayama also draws parallels to his current startup, Uplift Labs.

feed.title: Putting Recent Market Volatility in Perspective
feed.summary: This article provides perspective on recent market volatility, noting that while 2022 has been a bumpy ride for investors with significant downturns in growth stocks and technology, such fluctuations are not historically uncommon. It examines the CBOE VIX Index and standard deviation data to show increased volatility, driven by inflation fears and rising interest rates, but emphasizes that market losses are a normal part of investing. The piece concludes by advising long-term investors to maintain their asset mix and avoid drastic changes unless retirement or significant near-term expenses necessitate a re-evaluation of their portfolio.

feed.title: Laying the Groundwork for EV Charging Capability
feed.summary: The article discusses the growing importance of electric vehicles (EVs) in the energy transition and the challenges associated with developing a robust EV charging infrastructure. It proposes various business models for oil and gas companies to adopt, such as franchise, charging host, and operator/full-service provider models, to meet the increasing demand for EV charging.
