The piece also outlines key design considerations for an effective charge point monitoring system (CPMS) to ensure reliability, scalability, and efficient monetization of charge points.

feed.title: Elon Musk blasts ESG after DWS office raids over greenwashing allegations
feed.summary: Elon Musk criticized the ESG industry once more after DWS's Frankfurt offices were raided due to greenwashing allegations. The Tesla CEO tweeted on June 1st that he had "yet to see an ESG list that *isn’t* fraudulent." This follows his previous strong remarks calling ESG "a scam" after Tesla was removed from the S&P ESG Index.

feed.title: Tesla Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. stock (TSLA) fell 0.18% to $758.26 on Tuesday, May 31, 2022, despite an overall poor trading session for the stock market. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high but outperformed some competitors, such as Toyota Motor Corp. ADR (TM) and Honda Motor Co. Ltd. ADR (HMC), although it lagged behind General Motors Co. (GM). Trading volume for Tesla exceeded its 50-day average.

feed.title: Jupiter Wagons Ltd. launches ‘Jupiter Electric Mobility’, enters the EV segment
feed.summary: Jupiter Wagons Ltd. has launched 'Jupiter Electric Mobility' (JEM) to enter the electric commercial vehicle market. This initiative involves a joint venture with EA GreenPower Private Limited, a subsidiary of GreenPower Motor Company Inc., aiming to produce LCV, MCV, and HCV categories in India and establish it as a manufacturing hub for global exports. The company plans to invest Rs 200 crores in the next three years, focusing on B2B distribution for logistics, e-commerce, and FMCG businesses.

feed.title: GM slashes prices of Chevy Bolt electric vehicles despite rising commodity costs
feed.summary: General Motors has significantly cut the prices of its 2023 Chevrolet Bolt EV and Bolt EUV models, making the Bolt EV potentially the most affordable electric vehicle in the U.S. This price reduction, enacted despite rising commodity costs and amidst price hikes from competitors like Tesla and Rivian, is an effort to improve competitiveness and align with customer purchase prices. The Bolt models, which use older battery technology, are expected to see a boost in sales, with production of the 2023 models resuming after a recall-related shutdown.

feed.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station Market Size to grow by USD 15.81 billion from 2021 to 2026|Driven by the Increasing Number of M & A and Strategic Partnerships to Drive Market | Technavio
feed.summary: The Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station Market is projected to grow by USD 15.81 billion between 2021 and 2026, accelerating at a CAGR of 20.65%. This growth is primarily driven by an increasing number of mergers, acquisitions, and strategic partnerships within the industry. However, market expansion could be hindered by a lack of standardization in EV charging infrastructure.

feed.title: Self-driving car companies' first step to making money isn't robotaxis
feed.summary: Self-driving car companies are finding their initial path to profitability not through robotaxis, but through sales of driver-assistance software. Investment analysts from Goldman Sachs and Nomura highlight significant opportunities in auto software, with companies like WeRide partnering with Bosch to develop mass-production assisted driving systems. This L2/L3 market, particularly strong in China, offers clearer commercial value and a quicker revenue stream compared to fully autonomous robotaxi services.

feed.title: Electric vehicle maker Stellantis will buy lithium produced at Salton Sea
feed.summary: Stellantis, a major electric vehicle manufacturer, has signed a 10-year agreement with Controlled Thermal Resources (CTR) to purchase battery-grade lithium hydroxide from CTR's Hell's Kitchen project at the Salton Sea. This deal aims to secure a low-carbon lithium supply for Stellantis' North American electrified vehicle production, supporting its ambitious goal of 5 million annual battery electric vehicle sales by 2030. CTR plans to produce lithium from geothermal brines using an environmentally friendly, closed-loop process.

feed.title: Who’ll be Europe’s next green billionaire?
feed.summary: This article examines the current "green billionaires" in European climate tech and identifies potential future candidates. It highlights founders like Denis Sverdlov (Arrival), Stephen Fitzpatrick (Ovo Group), and Peter Carlsson (Northvolt), detailing their net worths based on company valuations and ownership stakes. The piece notes the dominance of fintech and software in creating wealth so far, but points to the rapid growth of the climate tech sector as a new frontier for high-value entrepreneurs.

feed.title: Chip shortage is easing, says world's biggest truck-maker Daimler Truck Holding AG
feed.summary: Daimler Truck Holding AG, the world's largest truck-maker, is observing positive signs of the global chip shortage easing. Despite the improving situation, the company is still closely monitoring the supply chain, as stated by Karin Radstrom, CEO of the Mercedes-Benz truck brand. While demand remains high and production backlogs are keeping factories busy, the company is also focusing on its zero-emissions plan, developing battery-powered and hydrogen fuel-cell trucks.

feed.title: Tesla Fair Fund distributions established to pay 'harmed' investors
feed.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission announced the establishment of the Tesla Fair Fund to distribute payments to investors harmed by Elon Musk's "funding secured" tweet. Investors who bought Tesla Inc. shares between August 7 and August 8, 2018, may be eligible for distributions. This fund was created after Tesla and CEO Elon Musk agreed to pay $40 million to settle an SEC lawsuit alleging the tweet was false and misleading.

feed.title: What Does Amazon's Stock Split Mean for Investors?
feed.summary: Amazon is executing a 20-1 stock split, its first in over two decades, effective June 3. The split will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate for Amazon to $192 per share from $3,850, but senior analyst Dan Romanoff's long-term view remains unchanged, anticipating continued growth in e-commerce, AWS, and advertising. Other major tech companies like Alphabet and Tesla are also planning stock splits.

feed.title: U.S. safety regulators receive over 750 complaints of Teslas braking for no reason
feed.summary: U.S. safety regulators have received over 750 complaints from Tesla owners reporting that their vehicles, operating on partially automated driving systems, suddenly stopped on roadways for no apparent reason. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is investigating these "phantom braking" incidents in Models 3 and Y from 2021 and 2022, covering an estimated 416,000 vehicles. This is one of several ongoing investigations and recalls for Tesla by safety regulators.

feed.title: Premarket Movers: Okta Cl A, HashiCorp Cl A, Kohl's Corp
feed.summary: This article details pre-market stock movements for several companies. Okta Cl A and Kohl's Corp saw significant gains, up 16.2% and 7.3% respectively. Other companies like BRP, PagSeguro Digital, and Nutex Health also recorded gains, while HashiCorp Cl A and Tesla experienced declines.

feed.title: Musk wants to cut 10 percent of Tesla jobs: Report
feed.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk reportedly has a "super bad feeling" about the economy and plans to cut about 10 percent of jobs at the electric carmaker, according to an email sent to executives. This message, titled "pause all hiring worldwide," follows his demand for staff to return to the workplace or leave, and comes amidst growing warnings from business leaders about a potential recession. The move has impacted Tesla's stock performance and is a more direct statement on the economic outlook than previous warnings from Musk.

feed.title: Amazon (AMZN) Gains as Stock Split Lowers Price Tag for Retail Buyers
feed.summary: Amazon's stock surged after a 20-for-1 split, making shares more accessible to retail investors. This marks the company's first split in over two decades, leading to increased trading volume and outperforming the Nasdaq 100 Index. The move is expected to attract greater retail interest, potentially acting as a sentiment catalyst.

feed.title: WalMart expands transportation partnerships with electric, hydrogen vehicle pilots
feed.summary: Walmart is expanding its transportation pilot programs to include electric, hydrogen, and natural gas-powered vehicles, partnering with companies like Cummins, Daimler Truck's Freightliner, and Nikola. These initiatives support Walmart's 2040 goal of achieving zero emissions across its global operations, which include a large fleet of tractors and trailers. The retailer emphasized that it is still in the testing phase, exploring multiple solutions, as no single technology currently provides a comprehensive path to decarbonization at scale.

feed.title: Enable Better Performance, Fuel Economy with Garrett’s Electric Compressor for Hybrid Vehicles
feed.summary: Garrett Motion has developed a new generation electric compressor (E-Compressor) for hybrid vehicles, designed to improve performance, enhance fuel economy, and reduce exhaust emissions. This technology can be integrated with 48-volt mild hybrids and 300-400-volt full and plug-in hybrids, expanding Garrett's presence in the growing hybrid market. When paired with a turbocharger, the E-Compressor provides "boost on demand," offering benefits like increased power density, torque density, and significant reductions in NOx and soot emissions, while also enabling fuel savings.

feed.title: ‘World Champion’ WM Motor Joins China EV Race to Market With Hong Kong Listing Plan
feed.summary: WM Motor, a Chinese electric vehicle maker, is seeking to raise up to $1 billion through a Hong Kong IPO, making it the fifth such company to list in the city. Despite aiming for a less crowded Shanghai market initially, WM Motor saw significant revenue growth, doubling unit sales in 2021, but also experienced increased losses. The company, which builds its own manufacturing facilities and focuses on mid-range EVs, faces stiff competition from established players and other startups in China's burgeoning EV market.

feed.title: Baidu's electric vehicle firm Jidu unveils first 'robot' car
feed.summary: Baidu's EV arm Jidu Auto has unveiled its first "robot" concept car, aiming for mass production in 2023. This vehicle, co-funded by Chinese automaker Geely, features Level 4 autonomous capabilities and voice recognition, and is designed to attract tech-savvy users. The move positions Baidu among global tech companies developing smart cars following Tesla's success.

feed.title: Tesla goes ahead with China hiring event after Musk job warning
feed.summary: Despite Elon Musk's recent warnings about job cuts and being "overstaffed," Tesla proceeded with a China hiring event on Thursday, adding two dozen new job postings. The event aimed to recruit staff for "smart manufacturing" roles, including managers and engineers for its Giga Press machines. This comes as Tesla's Shanghai plant, a significant contributor to its global production and revenue, plans to expand, even after being impacted by recent COVID-19 lockdowns.

feed.title: Stellantis Stock Is Undervalued, Even as It Catches Up in the Electric Vehicle Market
feed.summary: Stellantis, formed from the 2021 merger of Fiat Chrysler and Peugeot, is making an aggressive push into the electric vehicle market after being a laggard. Despite its efforts to catch up, Morningstar analysts consider Stellantis stock undervalued, trading at a significant discount to its peers. The company plans an all-electric lineup for its luxury brands by 2024 and aims for 50% EV sales in North America by 2030, alongside ambitious carbon reduction and revenue growth targets.

feed.title: U.S. agency upgrades Tesla Autopilot safety probe, step before possible recall
feed.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has upgraded its probe into 830,000 Tesla vehicles equipped with Autopilot, moving closer to a potential recall. The agency is investigating the system's performance after numerous crashes involving emergency vehicles and is focusing on whether Tesla adequately ensures drivers pay attention while using the assistance feature. This upgrade to an engineering analysis is a crucial step before NHTSA can demand a recall.

feed.title: Renewable energy bill threatens to stall solar in Hawaii
feed.summary: Solar workers and clean energy advocates in Hawaii are urging Governor Ige to veto SB 2510, a bill that mandates one-third of renewable energy to come from “firm” sources, rather than intermittent ones like solar and wind. Opponents argue this bill would harm the solar industry, raise consumer costs, and favor expensive biomass or biofuel projects. Supporters of the bill express concern about over-reliance on intermittent energy, while critics believe it jeopardizes the state's clean energy goals and might be influenced by special interests.

feed.title: ST continues to grow in Morocco – opens new clean room
feed.summary: STMicroelectronics has opened a new clean room at its Bouskoura, Morocco location, dedicated to silicon carbide products. The company invested USD 240 million between 2020 and 2022 to expand capacity for the electric vehicle (EV) and industrial markets, creating 700 new jobs since July 2021. This expansion significantly increases the production capabilities for STPOWER Silicon Carbide products, which are crucial for EV applications.

feed.title: Trudeau meets Google boss Sundar Pichai, but no word on whether the tech CEO chewed out the PM over Bill C-18
feed.summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet (Google's parent company), but it's unclear if Bill C-18, a controversial Canadian media compensation bill, was discussed. The bill, criticized by experts like Michael Geist as a "shakedown," aims to make platforms like Google pay for linking to news content, giving the CRTC greater oversight. Google's Canadian head of public policy, Colin McKay, has stated that while Google supports journalism funding, Bill C-18 "would fundamentally and negatively impact millions of Canadians."

feed.title: Royal Caribbean wants to add Elon Musk's Starlink high-speed internet to its cruise ships
feed.summary: Royal Caribbean is seeking FCC approval to implement Elon Musk's Starlink high-speed internet on its cruise ships to significantly enhance onboard connectivity. This move aims to address current internet limitations and improve guest experience and business operations at sea. The adoption hinges on SpaceX receiving regulatory approval to operate Starlink on moving vehicles.

feed.title: Apple’s New CarPlay Is the Foreshock to Releasing Its Own Vehicle
feed.summary: Apple's redesigned CarPlay interface, unveiled at WWDC 2022, is seen as a precursor to the company eventually releasing its own vehicle. The article also touches on other Apple developments from WWDC 2022, including its new multitasking system, the absence of tvOS, and hints about an upcoming AR/VR headset. This reflects a broader expectation that Apple is laying the groundwork for a future in automotive technology.

feed.title: Roku, Tesla, and Other Cathie Wood Favorites Are Falling
feed.summary: Cathie Wood's $12 billion flagship exchange-traded fund experienced a decline in Monday trading, signaling continued pressure on "innovation stocks" like Roku and Tesla. This event highlights the ongoing challenges faced by popular growth-oriented investments favored by the Ark Invest CEO.

feed.title: Enovix 3D Silicon Lithium-ion Batteries for EVs Can Achieve 98% Charge Capacity in Under 10-Minutes
feed.summary: Enovix has developed 3D Silicon Lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles (EVs) that can charge from 0-80% in 5.2 minutes and reach over 98% capacity in under 10 minutes. This technology not only offers rapid charging but also maintains a high cycle life, potentially accelerating the mass adoption of EVs by meeting and exceeding OEM roadmaps for faster charging capabilities. Co-founder and CEO Harrold Rust emphasized that this innovation addresses the demand for longer-range batteries and increased access to fast chargers for EV drivers.

feed.title: 7 Founder-Led Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever
feed.summary: This article highlights seven founder-led stocks, including Tesla, Nvidia, Salesforce, Blackstone, Steel Dynamics, Block, and Apollo Global Management, that are considered strong long-term buys due to their history of outperformance. The author emphasizes the sustained engagement of founders in their companies and provides a brief overview of each company's financial health, leadership, and recent performance. The piece suggests that founder-led companies tend to outperform those without a founder in the CEO role.

feed.title: Caterpillar headquarters leaving Illinois after nearly 100 years
feed.summary: Caterpillar Inc. is moving its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, Texas, after nearly 100 years in its home state. The construction equipment manufacturer previously moved its base from Peoria, Illinois, to Deerfield in 2017. This move follows a trend of major corporations, including Boeing and several tech companies, relocating headquarters to Texas.

feed.title: Royal Caribbean may add Elon Musk's Starlink internet service to its cruise ships
feed.summary: Royal Caribbean Group is exploring a partnership with Elon Musk's SpaceX to bring Starlink internet service to its cruise ships. The cruise line operator believes Starlink could significantly improve guest experience and business operations at sea, addressing current bandwidth constraints. This potential collaboration, if approved by the FCC, would be a first for the cruise industry and could set a new standard for internet connectivity on vessels.

feed.title: Caterpillar to move global headquarters from Illinois to Texas
feed.summary: Caterpillar Inc. announced it is moving its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, Texas. The company declined to state the reason for the move or if it received incentives, though Texas is known for lower labor costs and less stringent regulation. This relocation follows a trend of other major manufacturers, like Boeing and Tesla, moving headquarters to Texas from other states.

feed.title: Caterpillar Moving Its Headquarters to Texas from Illinois
feed.summary: Caterpillar Inc., the construction equipment manufacturer, announced its decision to move its global headquarters from Deerfield, Illinois, to Irving, a suburb of Dallas, Texas. This marks another major corporate relocation from the Chicago area, following Boeing's recent move. CEO Jim Umpleby stated that the move is in the company's best strategic interest, and the transition will begin this year.

feed.title: 2023 Genesis GV60 Quick Spin: Electrifying Performance
feed.summary: The 2023 Genesis GV60 is a new all-electric luxury SUV combining hatchback and four-door-coupe styling with impressive performance. The Performance trim boasts 429 hp, an adaptive suspension, and unique features like a Boost Mode for increased power. While offering quiet sportiness and a user-friendly interior, it has minor drawbacks such as restricted rear visibility and potentially difficult-to-decipher backlit buttons.

feed.title: New EV Battery Reaches 98 Percent Capacity in Less Than Ten Minutes
feed.summary: Enovix has developed a new silicon-anode lithium-ion battery for electric vehicles that can charge to 80% in 5.2 minutes and 98% in 10 minutes. This technology, called 3D Silicon, uses silicon anodes which offer higher storage capacity than traditional graphite while mitigating swelling issues with a proprietary constraint system. The company estimates these batteries will last at least 10 years, even after 1,000 charge cycles, addressing key concerns for EV adoption.

feed.title: Caterpillar to relocate global headquarters from Illinois to Irving, Texas
feed.summary: Caterpillar Inc. announced it will move its global headquarters from Illinois to its existing office in Irving, Texas, starting in 2022. This relocation adds Caterpillar to the growing list of Fortune 500 companies moving to Texas, bringing the total number of corporate headquarters in the state to 54. Despite the move, Illinois will continue to have the largest concentration of Caterpillar employees worldwide.

feed.title: Standard Mileage Rates for Business, Medical, and Moving Expense Purposes Will Increase in July
feed.summary: The IRS has announced a midyear increase in standard mileage rates for business, medical, and moving expenses, effective July 1, 2022. The business rate increases to 62.5 cents per mile, while medical and moving expense rates rise to 22 cents per mile. This adjustment, unusual for a midyear change, reflects recent increases in gasoline prices.

feed.title: Tesla to charge more for cars in United States as inflation bites
feed.summary: Tesla Inc. has once again increased prices for all its car models in the United States, with some models seeing prices rise by as much as $3,000, in response to persistent global supply-chain problems and soaring raw material costs. This marks the fourth price hike for some models in the US in 2022 due to rising costs of materials like aluminum and lithium, as well as an industry-wide chip shortage. Rival Rivian Automotive Inc. has also raised prices for new orders, and CEO Elon Musk has expressed concerns about the economy and the need for job cuts.

feed.title: Opportunities in US stock market for investors who want to invest in climate change theme
feed.summary: This article explores investment opportunities in the US stock market for those interested in the climate change theme, emphasizing the role of companies in mitigating climate risks and achieving long-term profitability. It highlights renewable energy, electric vehicles, and climate-focused Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) as key investment avenues. The piece also provides specific company examples and discusses market growth projections for the renewable energy sector.

feed.title: Tesla prices rise by thousands, again: Model Y now starts at $67,190
feed.summary: Tesla has once again raised prices for several of its models in the U.S. market, with hikes ranging from $2,000 to $6,000. The Model Y's base price increased by $3,000 to $67,190, while the Model S and Model X also saw significant price increases. These adjustments are attributed to intense demand outpacing production capabilities and ongoing supply-chain issues.

feed.title: If you can’t beat ‘em, join ‘em? Dominion Energy begins selling residential solar
feed.summary: Dominion Energy, historically resistant to residential solar, has launched BrightSuite, a subsidiary selling solar arrays to consumers. This move follows the expansion of onsite solar opportunities in Virginia and a significant increase in residential solar installations. While Dominion's brand recognition offers a competitive edge, its higher pricing may benefit independent installers as consumers comparison shop, potentially growing the overall distributed solar market.

feed.title: Sony and Honda Join Forces to Launch New EV Company, Targets Sales by 2025
feed.summary: Sony and Honda have officially formed Sony Honda Mobility Inc., a new electric vehicle joint venture, with plans to start selling high-value EVs and mobility services by 2025. This collaboration brings together Honda's vehicle manufacturing and environmental technologies with Sony's expertise in imaging, sensing, telecommunication, network, and entertainment technologies. The initiative aligns with Honda's broader environmental goals, including achieving carbon neutrality and 100% EV sales by 2040.

feed.title: Ariana Grande Debuts Chapter 3 of R.E.M. Beauty with a Bang(s)
feed.summary: Ariana Grande's R.E.M. Beauty launched its third collection, 'Chapter 3: on your collar,' focusing on lip products. This collection, which includes five new formulas like lip oil, balm, liner, and lipsticks, follows the brand's 'drops' model and continues its extraterrestrial aesthetic. R.E.M. Beauty's initial collections, Chapters 1 and 2, are also available at Ulta stores.

feed.title: Elon Musk and Tesla sued over Dogecoin ‘pyramid scheme’
feed.summary: Elon Musk and Tesla are being sued for $258 billion by a Dogecoin investor who alleges they ran a pyramid scheme to inflate the cryptocurrency's value. The plaintiff, Keith Johnson, claims Musk manipulated Dogecoin for "profit, exposure and amusement" despite knowing it had no intrinsic value, and seeks damages for the $86 billion decline in Dogecoin's market value since May 2021. Johnson also wants to prevent Musk and his companies from promoting Dogecoin and to have it declared gambling under federal and New York law.

feed.title: How the massive EV transition is starting in the car rental industry
feed.summary: The car rental industry is undergoing a significant transition to electric vehicles (EVs), led by Hertz's substantial purchase of Teslas, followed by moves from Enterprise and Avis. This shift, however, faces challenges such as limited EV availability, insufficient charging infrastructure, and the need to educate both employees and customers. Despite these hurdles, rental companies are targeting corporate clients who seek to meet ESG goals through EV adoption, and the industry is seen as crucial for broader public exposure to EVs.

feed.title: Mining billionaire Robert Friedland launches IPO for Ivanhoe Electric
feed.summary: Billionaire Robert Friedland is launching an initial public offering (IPO) for Ivanhoe Electric Inc., aiming to raise US$180-million. The Vancouver-based company will focus on supplying copper and other critical minerals for electric cars and clean-energy technology, with properties in Arizona and Utah. This IPO marks a significant event in a quiet market, with shares planned for listing on both the Toronto and New York stock exchanges.

feed.title: Why ESG is Becoming a Bigger Deal for Investors
feed.summary: ESG (environmental, social, and governance) investing is rapidly gaining traction, with a record $649 billion poured into ESG-focused funds in 2021. Major players like BlackRock are emphasizing ESG, believing that companies deliberating on their societal role perform better, leading to long-term value for shareholders. While greenwashing concerns exist, new global standards and regulatory clarifications are emerging as ESG becomes a mainstream method for evaluating businesses and attracting investment.

feed.title: Laid-Off Workers Claim Tesla Violated WARN Act in Suit
feed.summary: Former Tesla employees have filed a lawsuit alleging the company violated the federal WARN Act by failing to provide 60 days' advance notice before mass layoffs. Two workers from Tesla's battery factory near Reno, Nevada, claim they were terminated without notice and are seeking class-action status for others affected by May and June job cuts. The plaintiffs are seeking compensation and benefits for 60 days following their termination.

feed.title: General Motors increases Hummer EV price by $6,250
feed.summary: General Motors has increased the price of its Hummer EV pickup truck by $6,250 due to higher commodity and transportation costs. The price increase will affect new orders, while the 77,500 existing reservations will not be impacted. This move follows similar price adjustments made by other EV manufacturers like Tesla and Rivian to offset rising supply chain costs.

feed.title: 2022 Cars.com American-Made Index: Which Cars Are the Most American?
feed.summary: Cars.com has released its 2022 American-Made Index, ranking vehicles based on assembly location, parts content, engine and transmission origins, and U.S. manufacturing workforce. Tesla dominates the top spots, with its Model Y retaining the #1 position and all four Tesla models in the top 10. The study also highlights increasing interest in electrified vehicles, despite inventory challenges, and details the methodology used to determine the rankings.

feed.title: 2022 Cars.com American-Made Index: What About the Least American Cars?
feed.summary: This article discusses the "least American" cars based on Cars.com's 2022 American-Made Index, highlighting vehicles that didn't qualify due to various factors like assembly location. It notes that many popular models from major automakers, including Ford and GM, are manufactured outside the U.S., and only Tesla currently produces all its U.S.-sold cars domestically. The piece also provides a breakdown of major automakers' share of U.S. light-duty sales from domestic assembly.

feed.title: Why You Might Buy Your Next Car Online (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Tesla's decision in 2019 to sell cars exclusively online, initially met with skepticism, has proven successful, forcing the auto industry to reconsider its traditional dealership model. This approach, adopted by other EV makers, could transform car sales, as consumers appreciate the convenience and service of online purchasing, potentially impacting established automakers and dealers.

feed.title: Tesla sued by former employees over 'mass layoffs"
feed.summary: Tesla is facing a lawsuit from two former employees who claim the company violated federal law by not providing advance notice for "mass layoffs" at its Nevada gigafactory. The lawsuit, filed on behalf of all former US Tesla employees laid off in May or June without notice, alleges that over 500 employees were dismissed. This legal action comes after Elon Musk announced plans to slash 10% of salaried workers due to predictions of an "inevitable" US recession.

feed.title: Tesla sued by former employees over 'mass layoff'
feed.summary: Former Tesla employees have filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging that its recent "mass layoff" violated federal law by not providing advance notice of job cuts. The lawsuit, filed in Texas by two workers terminated from Tesla's Nevada gigafactory, seeks class action status for all affected employees and highlights the company's alleged failure to adhere to the 60-day notification period required by the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has dismissed the lawsuit as "trivial," while the employees' attorney emphasized the impact of these terminations on workers who received minimal severance.

feed.title: ATS Automation lands $90 million contract with EV manufacturer
feed.summary: ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc. has secured a US$70 million (C$90 million) contract with a global electric vehicle manufacturer to design and build fully automated battery assembly systems. This order, which will be recorded in Q1 fiscal 2023 and delivered over 18 months, is part of a multi-phase program for the EV company's North American operations. ATS CEO Andrew Hider highlighted that this leverages their experience in the EV market and strengthens their position as a leader in the growing sector.

feed.title: It’s time to talk about consolidation in the EV charging industry
feed.summary: The EV charging industry is undergoing significant consolidation, driven by President Biden's $7.5 billion infrastructure bill. Companies like Blink Charging are making strategic acquisitions, such as SemaConnect, to expand their networks and comply with "Buy American" mandates, which will allow them to access federal funding. Foreign companies like Schneider Electric are also increasing their footprint in the U.S. through M&A, indicating a trend toward strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and scaling DC Fast charging solutions.

feed.title: NIO Inc. ADR rises Tuesday, outperforms market
feed.summary: NIO Inc. ADR (NIO) saw a significant rise of 9.10% on Tuesday, closing at $22.66 and outperforming the broader market, including the NASDAQ Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average. This marked its second consecutive day of gains, although it remained $32.47 below its 52-week high. The company's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Tesla, Toyota, and Ferrari, which also saw gains.

feed.title: Tesla worker rejects $15 million payout in race bias lawsuit
feed.summary: A former Black elevator operator at Tesla's Fremont plant, Owen Diaz, has rejected a $15 million award in his racial abuse lawsuit, opting for a new trial. The original jury award of $137 million was significantly reduced by a federal judge, which Diaz's lawyers argue is unjust and insufficient to deter future misconduct by Tesla. This decision comes amidst other lawsuits against Tesla regarding alleged widespread race discrimination and sexual harassment at its factory.

feed.title: Tesla Model Y nabs title of most American-made 2022 model
feed.summary: Tesla's Model Y and Model 3 secured the top two spots on Cars.com's 2022 American-Made Index, with all four Tesla models landing in the top 10. The company's regional manufacturing approach and 100% domestic production for U.S. sales were key factors. General Motors, Honda, Toyota, and Ford also had significant representation in the overall index, and increasing consumer interest in American-made vehicles is noted, especially concerning EVs.

feed.title: SIGMA LITHIUM SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASES TOTAL NI 43-101 MINERAL RESOURCE BY ~50% TO 86 MILLION TONNES, ADDING 27 MILLION TONNES OF HIGH-GRADE 1.49% LITHIUM OXIDE IN PHASE 3
feed.summary: Sigma Lithium announced a 50% increase in its total NI 43-101 mineral resource to 85.7 million tonnes, primarily due to the addition of 26.8 million tonnes of high-grade 1.49% lithium oxide from its Phase 3 NDC deposit. This significantly strengthens the company's Grota do Cirilo Project as a major source of Battery Grade Sustainable Lithium, with Phase 1 construction remaining on schedule for commissioning by December 2022. The increased resource aims to further boost the potential production profile for global electric vehicle markets.

feed.title: How the Tesla Model S Changed the World
feed.summary: The article reflects on the 10th anniversary of the Tesla Model S, highlighting its transformative impact on the automotive industry by redefining electric vehicles and challenging traditional car manufacturing and sales models. It discusses how the Model S pioneered online sales, over-the-air updates, and robust performance for EVs, but also touches on the controversies surrounding Tesla's pursuit of full self-driving technology and its effects on the car's reputation. Despite challenges with reliability and CEO Elon Musk's public image, the Model S is recognized as a historically significant vehicle that fundamentally reshaped consumer expectations and industry practices.

feed.title: Elon Musk Says New Tesla Plants Are Losing Billions
feed.summary: Elon Musk has revealed that Tesla's new Gigafactories in Germany and Texas are currently incurring "billions of dollars" in losses as the company struggles to ramp up production. Supply chain disruptions, including COVID-19 lockdowns in China, have significantly hampered manufacturing efforts, particularly for Model Y SUVs with new battery technology. Musk emphasized the significant effort required to bring these factories to high-volume production.

feed.title: Musk says Tesla's new car factories 'losing billions of dollars'
feed.summary: Elon Musk stated that Tesla's new factories in Texas and Berlin are "losing billions of dollars" due to production struggles. These issues stem from battery shortages and logistical challenges like parts being stuck in Chinese ports, exacerbated by COVID-19 shutdowns. Despite these hurdles, Musk expects these problems to be resolved quickly, with production of the Cybertruck anticipated to begin in mid-2023.

feed.title: Billionaire Larry Ellison, among world’s richest people, bought Florida estate for $173 million
feed.summary: Billionaire Larry Ellison, co-founder of Oracle, has purchased a sprawling 22-acre estate in Manalapan, Florida for $173 million, marking the largest residential sale ever in the state. The property includes a portion of Bird Island and was bought from fellow software billionaire Jim Clark. The article also details Ellison's net worth, his role at Oracle, his ties to Tesla, his charitable contributions, and a controversial call he reportedly participated in regarding the 2020 presidential election.

feed.title: Tesla’s Texas, Berlin factories ‘losing billions of dollars’
feed.summary: Elon Musk has stated that Tesla's new factories in Texas and Berlin are "losing billions of dollars" due to struggles in ramping up production. This challenge is attributed to a shortage of batteries and port issues in China, along with supply chain interruptions exacerbated by COVID-19 shutdowns in Shanghai. Musk highlighted the company's overwhelming concern as keeping factories operational to avoid bankruptcy.

feed.title: Toyota recalls electric car for faulty wheel that may detach
feed.summary: Toyota has issued a global recall for 2,700 bZ4X electric crossover vehicles due to a potentially faulty wheel that could detach. The cause of the issue is still under investigation, and customers are advised not to drive the vehicles until a remedy is available. This recall poses a significant setback for Toyota's ambitious plans to expand its electric vehicle lineup, which includes having 30 EV models by 2030.

feed.title: Tech layoffs up, job offers gone, but much hiring
feed.summary: Despite a rise in tech layoffs and rescinded job offers, the tech job market continues to see significant hiring, driven by high demand for skilled workers and ongoing growth within the sector. While some companies are cautious due to recession prospects, many are still adding staff and retaining knowledge workers, with the tech industry historically outperforming other sectors during economic downturns.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Companies Paying Employees Who Travel for Abortions
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it would cover travel expenses for employees needing to travel out of state for abortions, expanding a benefit that covers services unavailable near an employee's home. This decision follows the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade and aligns JPMorgan with other companies like Citigroup, Starbucks, Amazon, Tesla, and Yelp making similar pledges. The move addresses the implications of state-level abortion bans, with many states poised to restrict or ban abortions following the ruling.

feed.title: Nearly 4 in 10 Who Bought a Car in the Past Year Have Regrets
feed.summary: A LendingTree survey reveals that nearly 40% of recent car buyers regret their purchase, with the most common regret being the vehicle's make and model. Younger generations and those who bought cars within the last year express more regrets, while baby boomers and long-term owners report fewer. Many high earners and men have taken action to address their regrets, such as selling or refinancing their vehicles, though a significant portion of consumers also struggle with car payments and being underwater on their loans.

feed.title: 2 killed as NIO electric car plummets 3 stories from building in China
feed.summary: Two people, identified as "digital cabin testers" for the electric car brand NIO, died when a vehicle plunged three stories from a Shanghai parking structure. The company stated the incident, which occurred on Thursday, was an accident and not caused by vehicle malfunction, and an investigation is underway. Photos from Chinese media showed the car on its side with a caved-in roof, surrounded by debris.

feed.title: Every new passenger car sold in the world will be electric by 2040, says Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods
feed.summary: Exxon Mobil CEO Darren Woods predicts that by 2040, every new passenger car sold globally will be electric, a significant shift from the 9% electric vehicle sales in 2021. Despite this projection, Woods states that the company, a major petroleum refiner, is adapting by focusing on chemicals, which can be used in EV manufacturing, and believes the transition will not "make or break" their business. Exxon Mobil is evaluating the impact of declining gasoline sales but expects to remain profitable, similar to its position in 2013-2014 even with reduced oil demand.

feed.title: Kroger increases EV charging offer across US stores
feed.summary: Kroger is expanding EV charging options across its US stores, partnering with Blink, Electrify America, EVgo, Tesla, and Volta. The grocery retailer plans to add hundreds more charging stations in various markets, building on the over 350 chargers already installed in ten states. While the company did not specify AC or DC breakdown, charging times are expected to vary, with many sessions averaging around 30 minutes.

feed.title: Wheels Up adds partnership with Hertz
feed.summary: Wheels Up Experience has forged a new strategic partnership with Hertz, offering its members access to Hertz’s electric vehicle fleet, including Tesla and Polestar models, available at private jet airport locations. Members will also receive complimentary President’s Circle top-tier status in the Hertz Gold Plus Rewards program, along with discounts and dedicated ground transportation assistance. This collaboration aims to provide a seamless door-to-door travel experience and expand Wheels Up's product offerings.

feed.title: BP, Shell to cover employee travel for treatment after Roe v. Wade
feed.summary: BP PLC has joined Shell PLC in committing to cover employee travel expenses for healthcare treatment following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade. Both European oil producers updated their healthcare plans to extend benefits for women needing to travel for services, though neither explicitly named abortion. This move comes as other major companies like Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, Tesla, and Walt Disney also updated their policies to cover travel costs for out-of-state abortion services, while U.S. oil majors have largely remained silent.

feed.title: Trading At A Mere 4x Earnings, Is VALE Stock A Buy?
feed.summary: This article analyzes whether VALE (NYSE: VALE), a major iron ore and nickel producer, is a buy given its current valuation of under 4x consensus 2022 earnings. Despite recent sequential declines in revenue and earnings due to intense rains and falling commodity prices, potential improvements in the Chinese economy and VALE's strategic focus on the EV market with deals like supplying Tesla, suggest an upside to its stock, which is valued at $25 per share. The company also appears to be in a stronger financial position having significantly reduced its net debt.

feed.title: Frito-Lay CHRO: 'Everyone needs mental health support' | Human Resources Director
feed.summary: Frito-Lay, a division of PepsiCo, Inc., is actively addressing the trucking industry's challenges, including high attrition and mental health concerns, by investing in its drivers' well-being. CHRO Patrick McLaughlin highlights the company's comprehensive approach, which includes competitive benefits, work-life balance initiatives, and robust mental health support programs like meQ and Spring Health. This strategy aims to improve retention and ensure Frito-Lay remains an employer of choice in a volatile labor market.
